simple.meaning: מַעֲרָב (maʻărâb) is a Hebrew word meaning “the west (as a region of the evening sun).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַעֲרָב (H4628) appears 14 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Chronicles 7:28, with occurrences in 1 Chronicles, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, Isaiah, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעֲרָב (H4628) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַעֲרָב (H4628) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַעֲרָב (maʻărâb) / H4628 is traced through 1 Chronicles 7:28, 1 Chronicles 12:16, 1 Chronicles 26:16, 1 Chronicles 26:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: Their possessions and settlements were Bethel and its towns, and eastward Naaran, and westward Gezer, with its towns; Shechem also and its towns, to Azzah and its towns;
Some of the children of Benjamin and Judah came to the stronghold to David.
To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman.
For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar.

Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, men of valor, one thousand seven hundred, had the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of Yahweh, and for the service of the king.
This same Hezekiah also stopped the upper spring of the waters of Gihon, and brought them straight down on the west side of David’s city. Hezekiah prospered in all his works.

Now after this, he built an outer wall to David’s city, on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, even to the entrance at the fish gate. He encircled Ophel with it, and raised it up to a very great height; and he put valiant captains in all the fortified cities of Judah.
As far as the east is from the west,
And gathered out of the lands,
Don’t be afraid, for I am with you.
that they may know from the rising of the sun,
So they will fear Yahweh’s name from the west,
As I was considering, behold, a male goat came from the west over the surface of the whole earth, and didn’t touch the ground. The goat had a notable horn between his eyes.

definitions.short: the west (as a region of the evening sun)
definitions.full: H4628. maarab or maarabah II. מַעֲרָב noun [masculine] west (late) (place of sunset); — מִמַּעֲרָבָה ( = בָ֯הּ , compare De Ges § 91 e ) Isa 45:6 from its setting-place (opposed to מִמִּזְרַחשֶֿׁמֶשׁ ); מַעֲרָב opposed to מִזְרָח also 43:5 ; 59:19 ; Psa 103:12 ; 107:3 , so ׳לַמּ westward 1Chr 7:28 ; 12:16 (van d. H. v. 12:15 ), 26:16 , 18 ; ׳מ opposed to מוֺצָא Psa 75:7 ; מִןהַּֿמַּעֲרָב (alone) Dan 8:5 ; with ה locative מַעֲרָ֑בָה 1Chr 26:30 westward , followed by לְ = to the west of 2Chr 32:30 ; 33:14 , ׳מִמּ לַגִּבְעָה Judg 20:33 according to ᵐ5 (not B) ᵑ9 Be GFM and others (see [ מַעֲרֶה ]). VI. ערב (√ of following; compare Arabic be black , crow (raven, rook, etc.); Assyrian ârivu, êribu ; Aramaic , עוְּרְבָּא , all crow, raven ).
definitions.rootNote: or (feminine) מַעֲרָבָה ; from 6150 , in the sense of shading ;
